question: In 1971, Apollo 14 commander Alan Shepard smuggled a modified club head to the Moon and became the first person to play which sport there?
Which burrowing Australian marsupial is the only animal known to produce cube-shaped droppings?
Bananas are very slightly radioactive, thanks to the naturally radioactive isotope of which chemical element they are famously rich in?

For nearly fifty years, Canada and Denmark fought the world's politest territorial dispute — the so-called Whisky War — by taking turns planting flags and leaving bottles of liquor on which tiny uninhabited Arctic island?
In 1945, engineer Percy Spencer noticed a chocolate bar melting in his pocket while he stood near an active radar set — an accident that led him to invent which kitchen appliance?
On the Pacific island of Yap, the traditional currency called rai takes the form of enormous carved discs — some wider than a car and far too heavy to move. What are these coins made of?
A newborn baby has roughly 300 bones, yet an adult has only about 206 — and not a single one is ever lost. What happens to explain the difference?
The All England Club, home of the Wimbledon Championships since 1877, was actually founded in 1868 for a completely different lawn game — which one?
Every summer, the Eiffel Tower measurably grows — by as much as 15 centimetres. What causes this seasonal growth spurt?

The mouth of one river at Lake Maracaibo sees so much lightning — on well over a hundred nights a year — that it's often called the lightning capital of the world. In which South American country is it?
Ancient Roman laundry workers whitened togas by soaking them in a liquid collected from pots on street corners — a trade so profitable that Emperor Vespasian slapped a tax on it. What liquid was it?

On the floor of the Gulf of Mexico, explorers have filmed actual underwater lakes — with distinct shorelines and rippling surfaces — resting on the seabed. What ingredient makes their water dense enough to pool beneath the ocean?
In January 1969, which band gave their very last public performance — an unannounced lunchtime concert on the rooftop of their London office building, broken up by the police?

Alfred Hitchcock's 1960 thriller Psycho is famous for its shower scene — but it broke a second Hollywood bathroom taboo, reportedly becoming the first major American film to show which everyday fixture actually being used on screen?
topic: Classic films and pop culture history

question: The largest known living organism on Earth sprawls under about nine square kilometres of forest in Oregon, USA — and it's neither a plant nor an animal. What kind of organism is it?

Eight years before Charles Lindbergh's celebrated solo crossing, two British airmen completed the first-ever nonstop transatlantic flight in 1919, ending it nose-down in an Irish bog. Name either of the two men.

In 1973, Motorola engineer Martin Cooper stood on a Manhattan sidewalk and made history's very first call of its kind — cheekily dialling his direct rival at Bell Labs to gloat. What kind of device was he holding?

In the Bering Strait, Big Diomede and Little Diomede sit less than 4 kilometres apart, yet the International Date Line runs between them — earning them the nicknames Tomorrow Island and Yesterday Isle. Which two countries do they belong to?

A well-known kitchen trick says a rock-hard avocado ripens much faster if you seal it in a paper bag with a banana. That works because ripening bananas give off which gas, which acts as a plant hormone?

In 1911, an Italian handyman walked out of the Louvre with a painting hidden under his coat, claiming he wanted to return it to Italy — a theft that made the artwork world-famous. Which painting was it?
Before it hit toy shelves in the 1950s, the squishy modelling compound Play-Doh was sold for a completely different job around the house. What was it originally used for?

In 1698, one ruler was so determined to drag his nobles into Western European fashion that he taxed their beards — even handing out tokens as proof of payment. Which famously reform-minded Russian tsar was it?
Despite its name, San Francisco's Golden Gate Bridge has never been painted gold. Its distinctive reddish colour — kept partly so ships can spot it in thick fog — has an official name. What is it?
Popcorn kernels explode because a small amount of something sealed inside each kernel suddenly turns to high-pressure steam when heated. What is that something?
An octopus's blue blood is pumped around its body by an unusual number of hearts. How many does it have?
On one planet in our solar system, a single rotation on its axis takes longer than a full trip around the Sun — its day is literally longer than its year. Which planet?
Thanks to far-flung overseas territories stretching from the Pacific to the Caribbean, which country spans twelve time zones — more than any other nation on Earth?

In the 1630s, the Dutch Republic experienced history's most famous speculative bubble, when a single rare bulb could briefly cost as much as a grand Amsterdam canal house. Which flower drove the frenzy?
The marathon's oddly precise distance of 42.195 kilometres dates from the 1908 London Olympics, when the course was stretched so the race could start on the lawn of which royal residence?
One living tissue in the human body contains no blood vessels at all and takes its oxygen straight from the surrounding air — which is exactly why it stays perfectly transparent. Which tissue is it?
In the pitch-black deep sea, the tiny male of which fish bites into the much larger female and permanently fuses with her body — living out his days as little more than an attached sperm supply?

High above powerful thunderstorms, ghostly red flashes called 'sprites' sometimes shoot upward toward the edge of space, lasting just a fraction of a second. What happening in the storm below triggers them?
Bone analysis of gladiators buried at Ephesus shows they ate a mostly plant-based diet — so dominated by one grain that Romans nicknamed them 'hordearii', meaning eaters of what?
When MTV went on air for the very first time in August 1981, it deliberately opened with a Buggles song whose title predicted exactly what the channel would do to an older medium. What was the song?

In the legendary shower scene of Alfred Hitchcock's 1960 thriller Psycho, the blood swirling down the drain looked terrifyingly real on black-and-white film — yet it was actually which sweet kitchen product?
topic: Classic films and pop culture history

question: Eight years before Lindbergh's famous solo crossing, aviators John Alcock and Arthur Brown completed the first nonstop transatlantic flight in 1919 — taking off from Newfoundland and ending nose-down in a soft bog in which country?

In the early 1990s, computer scientists at the University of Cambridge invented the world's first webcam for a very practical reason: to spare themselves pointless trips down the corridor. What everyday object was the camera pointed at?

Hemoglobin gets its punch from a single iron atom at the heart of the molecule. Chlorophyll, the green pigment in plants, has a remarkably similar structure — but which metal sits at its center instead?
A giraffe's neck can be over two metres long, yet it contains exactly the same number of neck vertebrae as yours. How many is that?
Tourists in London point at the clock tower of the Palace of Westminster and call it Big Ben — but strictly speaking, Big Ben is the name of what?

Point Nemo in the South Pacific is the spot in the ocean farthest from any land — more than 2,600 kilometres in every direction. Because nobody is ever nearby, space agencies use it as a deliberate crash zone for what?
Every so often, parts of Europe wake up to eerie 'blood rain' that leaves cars and snow coated in a reddish film. This colour comes from dust swept thousands of kilometres north from which desert?
When you mix baking soda with vinegar and it fizzes up dramatically, which gas is being released in all those bubbles?
The cheetah gets all the glory, but the true speed record for any animal on Earth — over 300 kilometres per hour — belongs to a bird of prey in its hunting dive. Which bird?
Founded in Kyoto in 1889 to make handmade playing cards, which Japanese company went on to become one of the biggest names in video games?
When the Mona Lisa vanished from the Louvre in 1911, French police hauled in a young Spanish-born painter living in Paris for questioning as a suspect. Who was he?

White chocolate contains cocoa butter, sugar and milk — but it is completely missing the dark component that gives milk and dark chocolate both their colour and their classic chocolatey taste. What is that missing component called?

In 2021, NASA's little helicopter Ingenuity made the first powered flight on another planet, on Mars. Tucked aboard as a tribute was a postage-stamp-sized piece of wing fabric taken from which pioneering aircraft?

Europe's very first paper banknotes were issued back in 1661 by a private bank in which country — one that, rather ironically, is today racing to become one of the world's first completely cashless societies?
Scientists warn that the wreck of the Titanic, resting almost four kilometres deep, may largely disintegrate within a few decades. What is slowly eating away its iron hull?
A desert is defined by how little precipitation falls, not by heat — which is why the largest desert on Earth is not the Sahara. Which continent holds the title?
Contrary to legend, the pyramid builders of Giza were not slaves but paid workers. Alongside bread, what drink made up a core part of their daily rations?
When the Washington Monument was completed in 1884, its very tip was crowned with a small pyramid of a metal that was then more precious than silver — but is dirt cheap today. Which metal?
In December 1965, two Gemini 6 astronauts smuggled a harmonica and sleigh bells aboard and played the first musical instruments in space. Which song did they perform?
An octopus's blood carries oxygen using copper instead of iron. What colour does that make its blood?
Only one country on Earth has its main territory spread across all four hemispheres — northern, southern, eastern and western. Which Pacific island nation is it?
The last Olympic gold medals made of solid gold were handed out in 1912. Ever since, they've been made almost entirely of a different metal, with just a few grams of gold plating on top. Which metal?

One place on Earth sees lightning storms on up to 160 nights every year — so reliably that sailors once used the flashes as a natural lighthouse. Over which large Venezuelan lake does this famous 'everlasting storm' rage?

Nearly 300 metres up the Eiffel Tower hides a small private apartment with wallpaper, wooden furniture and a grand piano — a retreat where its owner once hosted Thomas Edison. Who had this secret flat built for himself?
That famously puffy pocket of gas in a bag of potato crisps isn't ordinary air — manufacturers use a specific gas because oxygen would turn the frying oil rancid. Which gas?

In 1911 the Mona Lisa vanished from the Louvre, stolen by a former museum worker who kept it hidden in his small Paris flat for over two years. He was finally caught when he tried to sell the painting in the country where he insisted it truly belonged. Which country?

Long before children squeezed it into shapes, Play-Doh was sold as a household cleaning product. In the era of coal heating, homeowners rolled the soft putty across one surface in particular to lift off the soot. What was it made to clean?
Queen Elizabeth II visited more than a hundred countries during her reign, yet she never once carried a document that every other British traveller must have. Which document?

When the Hoover Dam was built in the 1930s, workers embedded hundreds of kilometres of steel pipes inside the structure and pumped ice-cold water through them. Without this trick, engineers calculated the dam would have needed over a century to finish doing what?
After six months floating on the International Space Station, astronauts return to Earth with up to five extra centimetres of something they quickly lose again. Five centimetres of what?

Chili plants make capsaicin to punish mammals, whose chewing teeth destroy the seeds. But one whole group of animals literally cannot feel the burn — and conveniently swallows the seeds whole and spreads them far away. Which group?
The name of the American dollar goes back to the 'thaler' — silver coins first struck in the 1520s in the mining town of Joachimsthal. In which present-day European country does that town lie?
Early jet airliners in the 1950s had square windows, but every passenger plane today has windows with rounded corners. Why did engineers make this change?
correct_answer: Sharp corners concentrate stress and crack

question: In 1957, the Soviet Union sent the first living creature into orbit around Earth — a small dog picked up from the streets of Moscow. What was her name?
How many hearts pump blood through an octopus's body?
On a hot summer day, the Eiffel Tower quietly gains up to 15 centimetres in height. What causes this seasonal growth spurt?
Nintendo, the video game giant behind Mario, actually started out making handmade Japanese playing cards. In which year was the company founded?
On which planet of our solar system does a single rotation on its axis — one day — take longer than a full trip around the Sun?
Every national flag on Earth is a four-sided rectangle or square — except one, shaped like two stacked triangles. Which country flies it?
Thanks to its far-flung overseas territories, which country spans more time zones than any other — twelve in total?
The shortest war in recorded history was over in under 40 minutes in 1896, when the Royal Navy shelled a sultan's palace. Which East African island state was Britain's opponent?
The guillotine feels like ancient history, but France used it for executions surprisingly recently. In which decade did the last guillotine execution in France take place?
The Eiffel Tower is up to 15 centimetres taller in summer than in winter — what causes this?
Which mythical creature is the official national animal of Scotland?
France's longest land border is not with Spain or Belgium — it is with which country?
In 1932, Australian soldiers armed with machine guns waged a famously unsuccessful military operation against which large flightless bird?
The 1896 war between Britain and Zanzibar is the shortest recorded war in history — roughly how long did it last?
Nintendo, the video game giant, started out in Kyoto making traditional Japanese playing cards — in which year was it founded?
Thanks to a chain of islands crossing the 180th meridian, which US state is at once the westernmost and, technically, the easternmost state?
In 1896, Britain fought the shortest war in recorded history — it was over in well under an hour. Its opponent was which island sultanate off the East African coast, today part of Tanzania?
On which planet in our solar system does a single day last longer than an entire year?
